title: Stream transaction boundaries and Tool Ambassador proposal
content:
Purpose
This doc proposes a set of API and SDK primitives for defining transactional boundaries within incremental streaming responses and for introducing a client-side "Tool Ambassador" pattern that brokers and mirrors tool invocations with a view toward low-latency hedging, offline replay, and clear structured-output commit semantics. It is intended as a focused, pragmatic PRD for a first implementation that balances rollout speed with safety and backwards compatibility.

Context and motivation
- Teams building complex agent-like flows are increasingly demanding: durable tool call semantics across intermittent networks, partial streaming outputs that can be committed or rolled back, and SDK ergonomics that make safe retries and offline replay straightforward.
- Current hosted streaming surface exposes incremental tokens and tool-call events but lacks a lightweight transactional model for: (1) expressing when a tool call should be considered authoritative (commit), (2) safely replaying partially delivered sequences, and (3) enabling client-side observation & local fallback proxies without leaking server invariants.

Key concepts introduced
- Stream Transaction Boundary (STB): an explicit marker emitted in the streaming channel indicating the logical commit point for a sequence of incremental frames. STBs are opaque IDs with optional human tags.
- Tool Ambassador (TA): a thin client-side component shipped as part of official SDKs (JS, Python) that manages: local mirrors of tool calls, speculative execution, idempotency keys, and offline buffering. The TA exposes a minimal API developers can adopt or replace with their own host logic.
- Mini-Saga pattern for toollets: short lived, bounded sagas (tool interactions) that are anchored to an STB and carry a compact compensating action signature for rollback when needed.

Goals
- Provide a clear commit model for streamed structured output so downstream systems can apply or ignore partial responses deterministically.
- Reduce accidental duplicate tooling side-effects when clients perform reconnects, retries, or speculative prefetches.
- Offer SDK surface that makes safe offline-first clients feasible without forcing teams to implement complex logic from scratch.

Non-goals
- Not aiming to replace full workflow orchestration engines (Temporal, etc.). This is for short-lived, low-latency tool interactions tied to a single inference session.
- Not implementing server-side saga orchestration; server remains authoritative for final commit decisions and will emit STBs.

User stories
- As a mobile developer I want the SDK to buffer tool calls when the user is offline and later reconcile with the hosted API without producing double-charges.
- As a backend engineer I want a deterministic commit marker so I can store partial semantic updates in my DB only when a Stream Transaction Boundary is observed.
- As an SRE I want telemetry that surfaces failed compactions and ambiguous tool-call idempotency conflicts so we can set meaningful alerts.

Proposed surface (high level)
- Streaming frame envelope additions (server):
  - frame.type: one of [text, structured, tool_call, stb, heartbeat]
  - frame.stb_id: present on frames that are part of a transaction block; absent frames are advisory
  - frame.commit_hint: optional short string ("final-summary", "action-confirm")
- STB lifecycle:
  - STB emitted by server to stream at the commit point 
  - STB contains: stb_id (opaque), sequence_range (first_seq,last_seq), checksum (optional), timestamp
  - SDKs must accept stale STBs and handle dup suppression using idempotency+sequence heuristics
- Tool Ambassador responsibilities (SDK):
  - Accept a tool_call frame and return immediately an ambassador-local idempotency_key
  - Mirror the tool invocation to a local durable store (in-memory+persisted cache on disk for mobile/edge SDKs)
  - Optionally execute speculative local toollets (for low-latency UX) and tag them as speculative until STB confirmation
  - On reconnect, reconcile local mirror with server acknowledged tool_call frames using idempotency_key and server-provided tool_call_id
  - Provide a small callback surface for developers to implement compensating actions if a mini-saga needs to be rolled back

SDK ergonomics and APIs (examples)
- JS SDK pseudocode (high level string):
  const amb = new ToolAmbassador({sessionId, storage: localForage});
  amb.callTool('pdf_extract', {url}, {speculative: true}) // returns {localId, ambStatus}
  amb.on('stb', (stbMeta) => { // commit handler });

- Python example (string):
  with ToolAmbassador(session_id) as ta:
      res = ta.call_tool('charge_card', payload, idempotency='kw-123', blocking=True)

Failure modes and mitigations
- Ambiguous replays: use combined (session_id + stb_id + client_seq) to map duplicates. If checksum mismatches, surface a conflict error and mark the toollet for manual reconciliation.
- Stale speculative outputs later contradicted by server: TA marks speculative outputs with a confidence flag and provides an onUpdate hook to downstream UI to replace/rollback content.
- Disk corruption of local mirror: implement journaling and tombstone markers; make the TA able to start fresh with a server-supplied reconciliation checkpoint.

Observability and telemetry
- New metrics:
  - stb_emitted_count, stb_latency_p50/p95 (time from first frame in a block to STB), stb_conflict_rate
  - ambassador_mirror_sync_lag, ambassador_replay_conflicts
  - speculative_promotion_ratio (what fraction of speculative tool results were confirmed)
- Traces: trace spans around tool_call->tool_backend->stb emission with id propagation through ambassador localId and server tool_call_id.

Security and privacy notes
- Tool Ambassador local mirror must respect customer data retention policies. By default TA uses an ephemeral cache; persistent mirror must be opt-in and encrypted by SDK with application-supplied keys where possible.
- STBs are opaque and do not carry PII; any structured frames included in the transaction should have explicit redaction markers.

Backward compatibility and migration
- Server will emit STBs alongside existing frames; clients that don't understand STBs simply ignore those frames.
- Introduce a capability advertisement header: X-Redwood-Client-Capabilities: stb,tool-ambassador-v1 so servers can enable certain behaviors per-client.

Rollout plan (phased)
- Phase 0 (experiment): internal SDK + experiment flag for select customers; collect metrics and edge cases.
- Phase 1 (beta): default STB emission for select streaming endpoints; publish SDK Tool Ambassador as beta package; add telemetry dashboards.
- Phase 2 (general availability): stable semantics, opt-in server-side enforcement for idempotency checks, documentation and migration guide.

Open questions and tradeoffs
- How strongly should server validate idempotency_key collisions vs leaving reconciliation to the TA? Tradeoff: stronger server validation reduces client complexity but increases server state and cross-customer attack surface.
- What is the right STB granularity? per-action, per-paragraph, or per-session? Recommendation: start per-action or per-logical-turn (configurable by route).
- Should speculative tool executions be limited to a sandboxed local runner provided by Redwood (security surface) or left to app devs? Default: SDK provides a sandboxed runner for common toollets; premium/enterprise customers can extend.

Next steps and action items (short list)
- Product: finalize public API sketch and capability header definition (owner: Priya) - due 2025-03-01
- Eng (serving-runtime): prototype STB emission in streaming infra + trace propagation (owner: Marco) - due 2025-04-01
- SDK: initial Tool Ambassador PoC in JS with basic local mirror and replay reconciliation (owner: Leah) - due 2025-04-15
- Legal/Security: draft data retention and encryption guidance for TA persistent mode (owner: Omar) - due 2025-03-20

Appendix: small examples and heuristics
- Idempotency heuristic: primary key = sha256(session_id || client_seq || amb_localid) - server maps to canonical tool_call_id and returns an acknowledgement window for safe replay.
- Compact STB example (JSON-like, shown as string): {"stb_id":"stb_01az","range":"345-359","ts":"2025-02-03T14:12:03Z","checksum":"b46f"}

Notes to reviewers
- This doc is intentionally implementation-oriented but light on precise wire formats; I want engineering feedback on cost/latency tradeoffs for storing STB state and on the scope of the Tool Ambassador responsibilities.
- Please add use-cases we missed where a short-lived saga pattern may be insufficient.

-- end of draft --
